headline: New York City Rent Hits a New High: Just in Time for the Class of 2026
summary: This year's college graduates heading to New York City for work are looking at the most expensive rental market the city has posted since Realtor.com® began tracking in 2019. The median asking rent climbed to $3,707 in the second quarter of 2026, up $164, or 4.6%, year over year. A studio apartment alone would consume 38.2% of a typical Computer Science graduate's starting New York City salary and 45.2% of a Business graduate's, according to the Q2 2026 NYC Rental Report from Realtor.com®.
